verdict.rationale: Gecko documents event-driven background automation. PR scans post pass/fail checks back to GitHub/GitLab on their own, Gecko re-verifies findings when a fix merges, it can commit fixes to a PR's head branch, and webhooks push events as scans run. Recurring scheduled scans exist only as a single API-reference mention ('manage scan schedules'), with no documentation of cadence, setup, or configurable automation rules, so user-defined background automation is thin. missing for 10: documented scan-schedule setup and cadence options, user-configurable automation rules or triggers beyond PR checks, independent or hands-on corroboration that background runs work unattended.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Gecko posts a pass/fail check back to GitHub or GitLab so reviewers see the security status inline.
When the fix merges, Gecko rechecks the finding and marks it **Fix verified** once the vulnerability is gone.
Gecko can commit the fix directly to the PR's head branch so the fix rides along with the change.
Gecko can push events to your systems as scans run and findings change
